immutable.proposition: The biblical God can be known not to exist even if the historicity of Jesus remains less certain.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Well, thank you. One minor correction, while I am convinced that Moses certainly did not exist, there's still some possibility I suppose that Jesus might have but I'm still evaluating that. It would seem that if there is or if there was a Jesus at best, he was a composite of multiple different characters. I honestly don't think that if you had a time machine that you would ever be able to find any one person you would be able to say was the historic Jesus but if you could find the historic Jesus then I think at best we would be able to just find him as a faith healer, really no different than any of the kind of faith healers we have wandering about now. He was just taking advantage of a different type of situation and demographic in that time but I think probably there was no historic Jesus. On the topic that they brought me to Arizona, they don't usually tell me what to talk about when they invite me to speak someplace although I'll have a clue whether it's going to be science, is it going to be secularism, is it going to be skepticism. In this case they specified that it was to be epistemology. They said they wanted me to talk about what we can and cannot say we know and I took an opportunity with that because as I said I had actually changed my position on this. I was an agnostic atheist when I began all of this a few years ago and I had since been convinced otherwise that it is possible to know that at least in terms of the Bible God that for certain that does not exist.

So how do you, as an atheist, account for their universality, their transcendent existence, which is not dependent upon the universe, not dependent upon the human mind? How do you account for their existence from your atheistic perspective? Would you agree that in a universe that is completely dead, that two rocks are still... Two rocks plus two rocks is still going to be four rocks? What you're doing is you are asserting a logical value right now about another condition. You're assuming the laws of logic. I'm asking you to account for them from your atheistic perspective. So if there is a universe in which there is no God, then two plus two still equals two. If there is no God, there is no universe. God's a necessary precondition. I'm trying to ask you to do something, and what you do is you dodge it.
